q: The burning wood in the air releases heat and ____ energies.
e: The burning wood in the air releases heat and light energies. Burning wood gives out heat and light as chemical energy is released.

q: Photosynthesis is the chemical reaction that occurs when plants use energy from the sun, carbon dioxide, and water to synthesise the ____ that the plant needs to survive.
e: Photosynthesis is the chemical reaction that occurs when plants use energy from the sun, carbon dioxide, and water to synthesise the food that the plant needs to survive. In photosynthesis plants use sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water to make food, and oxygen comes out as a product.

q: Whenever a chemical reaction (chemical change) occurs, energy is usually transferred to or from the ____.
e: Whenever a chemical reaction (chemical change) occurs, energy is usually transferred to or from the surroundings. The surroundings are everything outside the reaction you chose to study.

q: Changing states of matter (physical change) also involve ____ changes.
e: Changing states of matter (physical change) also involve energy changes. Physical state changes still move energy even though the substance stays the same chemically.

q: There are various kinds of energy such as kinetic energy (due to the movement), potential energy (due to the position), electrical energy, light energy, thermal energy, chemical energy, ____ energy, etc.
e: There are various kinds of energy such as kinetic energy (due to the movement), potential energy (due to the position), electrical energy, light energy, thermal energy, chemical energy, mechanical energy, etc. Mechanical is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: In addition, energy can neither be created nor destroyed as stated in the Law of Conservation of ____.
e: In addition, energy can neither be created nor destroyed as stated in the Law of Conservation of Energy. Physical state changes still move energy even though the substance stays the same chemically.

q: However, energy can change from one form to another without a net loss or gain of energy and it is called energy ____.
e: However, energy can change from one form to another without a net loss or gain of energy and it is called energy transformation. Transformation is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: electric motor (electrical energy into ____ energy)
e: Electric motor (electrical energy into kinetic energy). Kinetic is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: hair dryer (electrical energy into ____ energy)
e: Hair dryer (electrical energy into thermal energy). Thermal is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: battery (chemical energy into ____ energy)
e: Battery (chemical energy into electrical energy). Electrical is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: automobile engine (chemical energy into ____ energy)
e: Automobile engine (chemical energy into mechanical energy). Mechanical is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: solar cell (light energy into ____ energy)
e: Solar cell (light energy into electrical energy). Electrical is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Chemical energy is the energy that is stored in the ____ of chemical compounds such as atoms and molecules.
e: Chemical energy is the energy that is stored in the bonds of chemical compounds such as atoms and molecules. Bonds is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Humans release this chemical energy during ____ and use it to power systems inside the body.
e: Humans release this chemical energy during digestion and use it to power systems inside the body. Digestion is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Plants store chemical energy in ____ formed during photosynthesis.
e: Plants store chemical energy in carbohydrates formed during photosynthesis. In photosynthesis plants use sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water to make food, and oxygen comes out as a product.

q: A chemical reaction involves the breaking of bonds in the reactants and the forming of bonds in the ____.
e: A chemical reaction involves the breaking of bonds in the reactants and the forming of bonds in the products. Products appear on the right of the equation and in the numerator of K.

q: Some reactions take place on their own under a given set of conditions, and some are needed to provide ____ for the reaction to proceed.
e: Some reactions take place on their own under a given set of conditions, and some are needed to provide energy for the reaction to proceed. Physical state changes still move energy even though the substance stays the same chemically.

q: A process that can take place on its own accord is called ____.
e: A process that can take place on its own accord is called spontaneous. A spontaneous process can proceed on its own under the stated conditions, but that does not always mean it is fast.

q: ____ processes need the energy to take place.
e: Non-spontaneous processes need the energy to take place. Non-spontaneous: a spontaneous process can proceed on its own under the stated conditions, but that does not always mean it is fast.

q: Adding a solution of dilute sulphuric acid to a solution of sodium hydroxide is an example of a ____ reaction because the reaction takes place without any energy being added.
e: Adding a solution of dilute sulphuric acid to a solution of sodium hydroxide is an example of a spontaneous reaction because the reaction takes place without any energy being added. A spontaneous process can proceed on its own under the stated conditions, but that does not always mean it is fast.

q: The reaction between magnesium and oxygen, and the reaction between copper and oxygen are both ____ reactions.
e: The reaction between magnesium and oxygen, and the reaction between copper and oxygen are both non-spontaneous reactions. A spontaneous process can proceed on its own under the stated conditions, but that does not always mean it is fast.

q: Iron rusting is exothermic and ____.
e: Iron rusting is exothermic and spontaneous. A spontaneous process can proceed on its own under the stated conditions, but that does not always mean it is fast.

q: When the ice melts at room temperature, that is a spontaneous and ____ process.
e: When the ice melts at room temperature, that is a spontaneous and endothermic process. The system gains heat, so delta H is positive.

q: When sulphuric acid is slowly poured into water, the flask or beaker becomes ____.
e: When sulphuric acid is slowly poured into water, the flask or beaker becomes hot. Hot is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Examples of exothermic reactions are burning candle, the combustion of a fuel, the neutralisation reaction, respiration, and ____ of iron.
e: Examples of exothermic reactions are burning candle, the combustion of a fuel, the neutralisation reaction, respiration, and rusting of iron. An exothermic reaction releases heat to the surroundings, so the enthalpy change is negative.

q: Exothermic reactions give out ____.
e: Exothermic reactions give out energy. Physical state changes still move energy even though the substance stays the same chemically.

q: In exothermic reactions, the energy of the product is ____ than the energy of the reactants because energy has been released during the reaction.
e: In exothermic reactions, the energy of the product is lower than the energy of the reactants because energy has been released during the reaction. Aufbau fills lower-energy orbitals before higher-energy ones.

q: When ammonium chloride is dissolved in water, the flask becomes quite ____ to the touch.
e: When ammonium chloride is dissolved in water, the flask becomes quite cold to the touch. Cold is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Examples of endothermic reactions are melting of ice, cooking an egg, evaporating liquid water, and thermal decomposition of ____.
e: Examples of endothermic reactions are melting of ice, cooking an egg, evaporating liquid water, and thermal decomposition of limestone. An endothermic reaction absorbs heat from the surroundings, so the enthalpy change is positive.

q: Endothermic reactions take in energy from the ____.
e: Endothermic reactions take in energy from the surroundings. The surroundings are everything outside the reaction you chose to study.

q: In endothermic reactions, the energy of the products is ____ than the energy of the reactants because energy has been absorbed during the reaction.
e: In endothermic reactions, the energy of the products is higher than the energy of the reactants because energy has been absorbed during the reaction. An endothermic reaction absorbs heat from the surroundings, so the enthalpy change is positive.

q: Energy changes in chemical reactions are caused by the making and ____ of chemical bonds.
e: Energy changes in chemical reactions are caused by the making and breaking of chemical bonds. Breaking is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: In a chemical reaction, bonds in the ____ must be broken first.
e: In a chemical reaction, bonds in the reactants must be broken first. Reactants appear on the left and in the denominator of K.

q: Energy is ____ to break bonds.
e: Energy is absorbed to break bonds. Absorbed is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Bond breaking is an ____ process.
e: Bond breaking is an endothermic process. The system gains heat, so delta H is positive.

q: Energy is ____ when new bonds form.
e: Energy is released when new bonds form. Energy is released when a gaseous atom gains an electron.

q: Bond making is an ____ process.
e: Bond making is an exothermic process. The system loses heat, so delta H is negative.

q: If the energy absorbed in bond breaking is less than the energy given out in bond making, the reaction is ____.
e: If the energy absorbed in bond breaking is less than the energy given out in bond making, the reaction is exothermic. The system loses heat, so delta H is negative.

q: If the energy absorbed in bond breaking is more than the energy given out in bond making, the reaction is ____.
e: If the energy absorbed in bond breaking is more than the energy given out in bond making, the reaction is endothermic. The system gains heat, so delta H is positive.

q: The total chemical energy of a substance is called its ____ (or heat content).
e: The total chemical energy of a substance is called its enthalpy (or heat content). Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: $H$ is the symbol for ____.
e: H is the symbol for enthalpy. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: The change in enthalpy describes the amount of heat transferred at constant ____ during a chemical reaction.
e: The change in enthalpy describes the amount of heat transferred at constant pressure during a chemical reaction. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: Heat changes can be measured by using a ____.
e: Heat changes can be measured by using a calorimeter. A calorimeter measures heat by tracking the temperature change of a known mass of water or solution.

q: The heat absorbed or released in a process occurring at constant pressure is called the enthalpy change; it is given the symbol ____.
e: The heat absorbed or released in a process occurring at constant pressure is called the enthalpy change; it is given the symbol deltaH. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: The unit of enthalpy change is kilojoule per ____ ($kJ mol^{-1}$).
e: The unit of enthalpy change is kilojoule per mole (kJmol-1). Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: In other words, $\Delta H$ is the difference in the heat content of products and ____.
e: In other words, deltaH is the difference in the heat content of products and reactants. Reactants appear on the left and in the denominator of K.

q: Enthalpy is not measured directly, however, the change in enthalpy is measured, which is the heat added or lost by the ____.
e: Enthalpy is not measured directly, however, the change in enthalpy is measured, which is the heat added or lost by the system. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: The change in enthalpy expressed as $\Delta H = H_{products} - $ ____
e: The change in enthalpy expressed as delta H = Hproducts - Hreactants. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: For an endothermic reaction where energy is absorbed from the surroundings, the total energy of the products is greater than that of the reactants, then $\Delta H$ is ____, i.e., a positive sign.
e: For an endothermic reaction where energy is absorbed from the surroundings, the total energy of the products is greater than that of the reactants, then deltaH is positive,, a positive sign. A positive enthalpy change means the system absorbed heat.

q: For an exothermic reaction where energy is released to the surroundings, the total energy of the products is less than that of the reactants, then $\Delta H$ is ____, i.e., a negative sign.
e: For an exothermic reaction where energy is released to the surroundings, the total energy of the products is less than that of the reactants, then deltaH is negative,, a negative sign. A negative sign marks heat leaving the system, or a falling concentration, depending on the equation.

q: The heat absorbed or released in a process occurring at standard conditions of temperature and pressure is called the standard enthalpy change, ____.
e: The heat absorbed or released in a process occurring at standard conditions of temperature and pressure is called the standard enthalpy change, deltaHdegrees. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: The standard conditions chosen for energy changes are as follows: standard temperature = $25^\circ C$ = ____ $K$
e: The standard conditions chosen for energy changes are as follows: standard temperature = 25degreesC = 298 K. Higher temperature means a larger fraction of particles have energy at least Ea.

q: and standard pressure = $1 atm$ = $760 mmHg$ = ____ $kPa$
e: And standard pressure = 1atm = 760mmHg = 101 kPa. 101 is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: A ____ equation is a balanced chemical equation that includes the physical states of all reactants and products and the standard enthalpy change ($\Delta H^\circ$ is negative or positive).
e: A thermochemical equation is a balanced chemical equation that includes the physical states of all reactants and products and the standard enthalpy change (deltaHdegrees is negative or positive). Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: The standard enthalpy change of a reaction ($\Delta H^\circ_r$) is the enthalpy change when the molar quantities of reactants stated in the chemical equation react to give products under ____ conditions.
e: The standard enthalpy change of a reaction (deltaHdegreesr) is the enthalpy change when the molar quantities of reactants stated in the chemical equation react to give products under standard conditions. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: The standard enthalpy change of ____ of a compound is the enthalpy change when one mole of a compound is formed from its elements under standard conditions.
e: The standard enthalpy change of formation of a compound is the enthalpy change when one mole of a compound is formed from its elements under standard conditions. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: Note that the state symbol for carbon is shown as "____".
e: Note that the state symbol for carbon is shown as "graphite". Graphite is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The standard enthalpy change of ____ is the enthalpy change when one mole of a substance (element or compound) is burnt completely in oxygen under standard conditions.
e: The standard enthalpy change of combustion is the enthalpy change when one mole of a substance (element or compound) is burnt completely in oxygen under standard conditions. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: Combustion reactions are always exothermic and the enthalpy changes are always ____.
e: Combustion reactions are always exothermic and the enthalpy changes are always negative. A negative sign marks heat leaving the system, or a falling concentration, depending on the equation.

q: The standard enthalpy change of ____ is the enthalpy change when solutions of an acid and an alkali react together under standard conditions to produce one mole of water.
e: The standard enthalpy change of neutralisation is the enthalpy change when solutions of an acid and an alkali react together under standard conditions to produce one mole of water. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: The neutralisation reaction is exothermic and the enthalpy change is ____.
e: The neutralisation reaction is exothermic and the enthalpy change is negative. A negative sign marks heat leaving the system, or a falling concentration, depending on the equation.

q: Experimentally, ____ is not measured.
e: Experimentally, deltaH is not measured. DeltaH is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The heat change, $q$, is measured by using the following equation: $q = $ ____
e: The heat change, q, is measured by using the following equation: q = mcdeltaT. McdeltaT is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: A ____ is a device to measure the amount of heat released or absorbed in reactions that occur in solutions.
e: A calorimeter is a device to measure the amount of heat released or absorbed in reactions that occur in solutions. A calorimeter measures heat by tracking the temperature change of a known mass of water or solution.

q: The enthalpy change of ____, $\Delta H_{sol}$, of a substance, is the enthalpy change when one mole of the substance is dissolved in water.
e: The enthalpy change of solution, deltaHsol, of a substance, is the enthalpy change when one mole of the substance is dissolved in water. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: The amount of heat needed to raise the temperature of one gram of water by one degree is known as the specific heat ____ of water and is given the symbol $c$.
e: The amount of heat needed to raise the temperature of one gram of water by one degree is known as the specific heat capacity of water and is given the symbol c. Specific heat capacity is the energy needed to raise 1 g of a substance by 1 degree Celsius.

q: If $\Delta T$ is positive value (i.e., $T_{final} > T_{initial}$), the ____ value will also be positive.
e: If deltaT is positive value (i.e., Tfinal > Tinitial), the q value will also be positive. Q is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Although $q = \Delta H$, the reaction is giving off this amount of ____.
e: Although q = delta H, the reaction is giving off this amount of energy. Physical state changes still move energy even though the substance stays the same chemically.

q: A ____ calorimeter is a type of calorimeter for determining the heat of combustion by igniting a sample in a high pressure of oxygen in a sealed vessel and measuring the resulting temperature rise.
e: A bomb calorimeter is a type of calorimeter for determining the heat of combustion by igniting a sample in a high pressure of oxygen in a sealed vessel and measuring the resulting temperature rise. A calorimeter measures heat by tracking the temperature change of a known mass of water or solution.

q: The highly accurate values of the standard enthalpy change of combustion ($\Delta H^\circ_c$) can be measured only by a ____ calorimeter.
e: The highly accurate values of the standard enthalpy change of combustion (deltaHdegreesc) can be measured only by a bomb calorimeter. A calorimeter measures heat by tracking the temperature change of a known mass of water or solution.

q: There are very few reactions whose enthalpy change can be measured directly by measuring the change in ____ in a calorimeter.
e: There are very few reactions whose enthalpy change can be measured directly by measuring the change in temperature in a calorimeter. Temperature is the one stress that can change the value of K.

q: In some cases, the reaction is difficult, even ____, to carry out individually.
e: In some cases, the reaction is difficult, even impossible, to carry out individually. Impossible is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: By using ____'s law, the enthalpy change for such reactions can be determined indirectly.
e: By using Hess's law, the enthalpy change for such reactions can be determined indirectly. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: The enthalpy change for a chemical reaction is the same, whatever ____ is taken from reactants to products.
e: The enthalpy change for a chemical reaction is the same, whatever route is taken from reactants to products. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: Hess's law can be illustrated by drawing an enthalpy ____.
e: Hess's law can be illustrated by drawing an enthalpy cycle. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: According to Hess's law, the enthalpy changes of Route I are the ____ as for Route II.
e: According to Hess's law, the enthalpy changes of Route I are the same as for Route II. Equal forward and reverse rates keep concentrations the same at equilibrium.

q: Note that the standard enthalpy change for the formation of an element in its standard state is ____ and no need to take it into account.
e: Note that the standard enthalpy change for the formation of an element in its standard state is zero and no need to take it into account. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: To determine the enthalpy change of reaction from enthalpy changes of formation, the corresponding ____ of reactant and product should be considered.
e: To determine the enthalpy change of reaction from enthalpy changes of formation, the corresponding elements of reactant and product should be considered. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: Firstly, write the balanced chemical equation for the standard enthalpy change of reaction at the ____.
e: Firstly, write the balanced chemical equation for the standard enthalpy change of reaction at the top. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: The elements are written at the bottom with arrows pointing ____ and balanced the elements.
e: The elements are written at the bottom with arrows pointing upwards and balanced the elements. Upwards is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: To determine the enthalpy change of formation from enthalpy changes of combustion, the corresponding combustion ____ should be considered.
e: To determine the enthalpy change of formation from enthalpy changes of combustion, the corresponding combustion products should be considered. Products appear on the right of the equation and in the numerator of K.

q: The combustion products (usually carbon dioxide and ____) are written at the bottom.
e: The combustion products (usually carbon dioxide and water) are written at the bottom. Water is often the solvent, the proton host, or a condensation product, depending on the stem.

q: Enthalpy changes are due to the breaking and ____ of bonds.
e: Enthalpy changes are due to the breaking and forming of bonds. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: Breaking a bond absorbs energy ($\Delta H$ is positive) and making a bond releases energy ($\Delta H$ is ____).
e: Breaking a bond absorbs energy (deltaH is positive) and making a bond releases energy (deltaH is negative). A negative sign marks heat leaving the system, or a falling concentration, depending on the equation.

q: The energy needed to make or break bonds is called bond energy (bond ____).
e: The energy needed to make or break bonds is called bond energy (bond enthalpy). Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: The higher the bond enthalpy, the more energy needed to break the bond, and the ____ is the bond.
e: The higher the bond enthalpy, the more energy needed to break the bond, and the stronger is the bond. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: The symbol for bond energy is ____.
e: The symbol for bond energy is E. E is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: So, $E(C-H)$ refers to the bond enthalpy of a mole of single bonds between carbon and ____ atoms.
e: So, E(C-H) refers to the bond enthalpy of a mole of single bonds between carbon and hydrogen atoms. Hydrogen here is the element or the proton being transferred in the chemistry of this stem.

q: The bond enthalpy for double and triple bonds refers to a mole of double or ____ bonds.
e: The bond enthalpy for double and triple bonds refers to a mole of double or triple bonds. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: When new bonds are formed the amount of energy released is the ____ as the amount of energy absorbed when the same type of bond is broken.
e: When new bonds are formed the amount of energy released is the same as the amount of energy absorbed when the same type of bond is broken. Equal forward and reverse rates keep concentrations the same at equilibrium.

q: Hess's law can also be used to find approximate values of enthalpy change of a reaction using bond ____.
e: Hess's law can also be used to find approximate values of enthalpy change of a reaction using bond enthalpies. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: In burning fuels (such as petrol, coal, propane, and butane) the ____ reaction take place during the reaction.
e: In burning fuels (such as petrol, coal, propane, and butane) the exothermic reaction take place during the reaction. The system loses heat, so delta H is negative.

q: The endothermic reaction takes place during cooking food, baking bread, boiling water and ____ the food.
e: The endothermic reaction takes place during cooking food, baking bread, boiling water and warming the food. An endothermic reaction absorbs heat from the surroundings, so the enthalpy change is positive.

q: A lot of weight loss applications use Hess's law concept to calculate the number of ____ burned during a workout.
e: A lot of weight loss applications use Hess's law concept to calculate the number of calories burned during a workout. Hess's law says the overall enthalpy change depends only on start and finish, not on the path you take.

q: Hand warmers produce heat from the exothermic reaction and Hess's law can help find out the total change in ____ and deduce how many amounts of each ingredient needed to keep warm for hours.
e: Hand warmers produce heat from the exothermic reaction and Hess's law can help find out the total change in enthalpy and deduce how many amounts of each ingredient needed to keep warm for hours. An exothermic reaction releases heat to the surroundings, so the enthalpy change is negative.
